messages.subject: error messages
parts:
Hi-
I am working with a dataset on birds counted along transects in an urban
area. We are using DISTANCE to estimate densities of each species. Some
runs have given us reams of error messages, a sample of which are shown
below. Generally there are no estimates produced either. Can anyone
interpret these for us? Thanks very much!

-- End of Analyis Engine Log File --
** Warning: Analysis engine wrote some output to the console error stream,
reproduced below. **
-- Start of Console Error Stream --
forrtl: error (63): output conversion error, unit 3, file C:\TEMP\dstD.tmp

forrtl: error (63): output conversion error, unit 3, file C:\TEMP\dstD.tmp

forrtl: error (63): output conversion error, unit 3, file C:\TEMP\dstD.tmp

forrtl: error (63): output conversion error, unit 5, file C:\TEMP\dstF.tmp

forrtl: error (74): floating underflow

forrtl: info (300): 1 floating underflow traps


-- End of Console Error Stream --
Analysis engine status 'Warnings'
Reading Results
Run finished

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: error messages
parts:
Hi Joan, list:

The forrtl: error messages come from the analysis engine, which is written in
FORTRAN. The output conversion error messages probably indicate a minor bug in
the program where some value it was trying to write to a file is longer than it
anticipated (e.g., an integer value of 1000 was being written in a space that only
had 3 characters reserved for it). The floating underflow error can safely be
ignored. I'm surprised that you got no estimates at all on account of these
errors. Anyway, send me a copy of your distance project and I'll check it out.

A general note to anyone sending distance projects to me (or anyone else): do not
just send the .dst file -- a project is composed of the project file (.dst) and
the project folder (.dat) (See online help, chapter 4). The best way to send them
is to use the Distance menu option File | Export Project... and then choose .zip
under "Save as". This packs both the project file and project folder into a .zip
file. For more, look in the online help index under "Exporting projects".

Cheers,

- Len
